characters.name: Pearl Casey
characters.arc: protagonist — wants to prove her worth beyond her father’s shadow —  — — Active Arc: Pearl chooses to burn her own dossier to protect Doyle, sacrificing her career’s safety for a moral imperative she didn’t plan.
characters.voice: sharp, clipped, uses humor as armor

characters.name: Sergeant Michael Doyle
characters.arc: supporting ally/NYPD — wants to keep his precinct clean but is bound by bureaucracy —  — — Active Arc: Doyle deliberately delays the arrest warrant for Elena Rossi, creating a window for Pearl to find the truth, driven by his own hidden guilt.
characters.voice: weary, gravelly, uses Irish lilt sparingly

characters.name: Silas Vane
characters.arc: supporting antagonist/Industrialist — wants to monopolize transit contracts —  — — Active Arc: Vane visits Pearl’s apartment unannounced to deliver a single spool of red thread, establishing his presence without violence, asserting dominance through intimacy.

characters.name: Lao Wei
characters.arc: supporting Chinatown apothecary — wants to protect his community from gang violence —  — — Active Arc: Wei identifies the silk cord as ceremonial wedding thread, not industrial waste, shifting the investigation from crime to ritual, forcing Pearl to rethink the killer’s motive.

characters.name: Elena Rossi
characters.arc: supporting immigrant seamstress — wants to feed her children —  — — Active Arc: Elena refuses to flee when offered protection, choosing to stand trial to clear her name, driving the climax by confronting the accuser directly.

characters.name: Man in Grey Coat
characters.arc: supporting antagonist/enforcer — wants to execute orders silently —  — — Active Arc: The Man in Grey Coat ambushes Pearl in the subway tunnel, not to kill her, but to steal a specific ledger page, revealing the true target of the conspiracy.

characters.name: Captain Halloway
characters.arc: supporting antagonist/corrupt official — wants to bury the scandal to protect political donors —  — — Active Arc: Halloway summons Pearl to his office and offers her a promotion if she drops the case, testing her integrity in a private, high-stakes confrontation.

settings.name: Chatham Square Signal Shed
settings.description: A rusted metal box overlooking the tracks, smelling of ozone and wet iron, where the foreman’s body was found.

settings.name: Pearl’s Apartment
settings.description: A small walk-up above a bakery, perpetually smelling of stale tobacco and lemon polish, cluttered with case files.

settings.name: Lao Wei’s Apothecary
settings.description: A dim shop in Chinatown, heavy with the scent of dried ginseng and damp earth, shelves lined with glass jars.

settings.name: The Elevated Train Car
settings.description: A rattling steel cage above street level, vibrating with the rhythm of the city, smelling of coal smoke and unwashed wool.

settings.name: Halloway’s Office
settings.description: A spacious room in Police Headquarters, air-conditioned by fans, smelling of peppermint and expensive leather, dominated by a large oak desk.

plot_points.description: Pearl finds the silk cord on the victim’s wrists, noting its unusual quality.
Lao Wei identifies the thread as wedding silk, hinting at a personal motive.
Pearl discovers the Pinkerton badge is a forgery linked to Captain Halloway’s donor.
Doyle is seen meeting with the Man in Grey Coat, suggesting betrayal.
Pearl confronts Halloway in the signal shed while the Man in Grey Coat attacks.
Doyle reveals he was being blackmailed by Halloway, providing the final evidence.
(resolution, ch15) Pearl arrests Halloway but loses her badge for acting outside protocol; Doyle is transferred.

voice: Close third, past tense, anchored in Pearl’s tactile and olfactory senses, with clipped rhythm and dry, observational wit.
